notes.meaning: God sent a message through the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, and Joshua, the high priest. The date was counted by the reign of the Persian king Darius because the Jewish people were back from exile but had no king of their own. Haggai spoke on a new moon feast day, when people gathered to worship. Both the political ruler and the religious leader were called to take the lead in serving God.

The people made excuses to put off rebuilding the Lord's temple, which was still in ruins. They claimed the right time had not arrived yet, perhaps thinking a prophecy about their years of exile was not fully finished. God called them 'these people' instead of 'My people' because their hearts were cold and selfish toward Him. They did not refuse to build entirely, but they kept delaying their duty.

God challenged the people through Haggai about their mixed-up priorities. They were living comfortably in houses finished with fine wood paneling while the Lord's house lay completely broken down. It was wrong for them to spend time and wealth on luxury for themselves while ignoring the place meant for God's worship.

The Lord told the people to stop and carefully think over their ways. The phrase literally means to set their hearts on their conduct and examine what was happening to them. God wanted them to see how their daily troubles were connected to their neglect of Him.

Nothing had gone well for the people because God was withholding His blessing. They sowed large fields but harvested very little food, and their drinks and clothes failed to satisfy or warm them. Their hard-earned pay slipped away as fast as if it were dropped into a bag full of holes. God brought this hardship on them to show that hoarding money while neglecting Him only brings loss.

God repeated His command for the people to think carefully about their ways. This second call was meant to turn their regret into immediate action. Real sorrow for sin must always lead to fixing what has been left undone.

The people were told to go to the nearby hills, cut timber, and rebuild the temple. God promised that when they built it, He would take pleasure in their worship and be honored among them. Doing what pleases God is the surest way to regain His favor and blessing.

The people looked for large crops, but their harvest was tiny, and God blew away even the little they stored. He asked 'Why?' to shake them awake and make them face the real cause of their misery. They were rushing about to improve their own houses while leaving God's house in ruins.

Because the people neglected God, the skies held back their dew and the ground failed to grow crops. The Lord Himself called for a drought that dried up the grain, wine, olive oil, animals, and the strength of the workers. God controls nature, and He used the dry weather as a warning to turn His people back to their duty.

Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the surviving remnant of the people listened to Haggai's preaching. They recognized that the prophet was speaking the very words of God, not his own opinions. A holy fear and deep respect for the Lord filled their hearts, which led them straight into obedience.

Haggai brought a tender, encouraging promise from the Lord: 'I am with you.' As soon as the people turned their hearts toward obedience, God shifted from words of warning to words of comfort. Having God with them gave them all the help, protection, and strength they needed to face their enemies and do the work.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Ancient readers sometimes mistook Haggai's title of 'messenger' to mean he was an angel in human form, but church teachers explained that he was an ordinary human prophet sent on God's mission.

notes.meaning: The Lord stirred up the spirits of the leaders and the people so that they were eager and willing to work. They came together and began working on the house of the Lord of Hosts, their God. True revival and willing service are gifts that come directly from the power of God's Spirit.

differ.view: People are spiritually sluggish and unable to obey God's word until the Holy Spirit first renews their hearts and makes them willing.

notes.meaning: The work on the temple began on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, just over three weeks after Haggai's first sermon. That short time was spent consulting, planning, and gathering wood and stone for the building. Once they realized their error, the people wasted no more time in getting down to work.
